title: 2020 Kenai Peninsula mid-air collision

agencies.name: National Transportation Safety Board
agencies.report_title: Aviation Investigation Final Report - Midair Collision

summary: A de Havilland DHC-2 Beaver and Piper PA-12 collided in mid-air on July 31, 2020, near Soldotna, Alaska, at approximately 1,175 feet mean sea level. Both aircraft were operating in Class E airspace with visual flight rules conditions. The DHC-2 was traveling northwest while the PA-12 was traveling northeast on converging flight paths. The PA-12 struck the DHC-2's left fuselage, causing the Beaver's left wing to separate. Both aircraft crashed, killing all seven occupants including Alaska State Representative Gary Knopp, the PA-12 pilot.
probable_cause: The failure of both pilots to see and avoid the other airplane. Contributing to the accident were the PA-12 pilot's decision to fly with a known severe vision deficiency that had resulted in denial of his most recent application for medical certification and the Federal Aviation Administration's absence of a requirement for airborne traffic advisory systems with aural alerting among operators who carry passengers for hire.

factors.evidence: The Piper, traveling northeast, struck the rear fuselage of the DHC-2 on the left side; paint transfer from the Piper was found on the DHC-2's aft fuselage (p. 3)

Both pilots failed to see and avoid the other airplane despite visibility study showing adequate visibility and time (12.5-53 seconds) for pilots to detect, judge collision course, and take evasive action (p. 1-3)

PA-12 pilot was denied medical certification in June 2012 due to open-angle glaucoma causing severe visual field loss; denial was upheld in July 2012; he had irreversible optic nerve damage and visual field defects in both eyes (p. 9)

PA-12 pilot had severely impaired peripheral vision and likely significantly diminished contrast sensitivity; complex background of broken clouds and sun at 84° azimuth within 20° of PA-12 track made DHC-2 harder to see (p. 1)
Two aircraft took off at same time from separate locations and collided three minutes later without any traffic coordination or communication (p. 1)

events.text: DHC-2 departed Longmere Lake bound for Cook Inlet. PA-12 departed Soldotna Airport bound for Fairbanks.
DHC-2 traveling northwest at 78 knots groundspeed, gradually climbing through 1,175 ft msl as it crossed Sterling Highway.
PA-12 traveling northeast at 1,175 ft msl, approximately 71 knots groundspeed, positioned north of and parallel to Sterling Highway.

Aircraft on converging flight paths in Class E airspace with visual flight rules conditions. Complex visual background with thin ceiling, broken-scattered clouds, mix of direct sun and shaded conditions.
DHC-2 becomes visible through PA-12 right window. PA-12 pilot should have been able to see DHC-2 for 12 seconds (until 08:25:51) but did not.
Collision occurs at 08:26:32.3 approximately 2.5 miles northeast of Soldotna airport at altitude of about 1,175 ft msl. PA-12 strikes DHC-2's left fuselage toward aft section.
Witness observed DHC-2's left wing separate and airplane enter uncontrolled, descending counterclockwise spiral before disappearing from view.
DHC-2 main wreckage heavily fragmented, located in wooded residential area. PA-12 wreckage located about 600 ft east at near vertical attitude.
All 7 occupants killed: 1 PA-12 pilot and 6 DHC-2 occupants (1 pilot and 5 passengers), including Alaska State Representative Gary Knopp.

recommendations.text: Require the installation of ADS-B Out- and In-supported airborne traffic advisory systems that include aural and visual alerting functions in all aircraft conducting operations under 14 CFR Part 135.

Require all pilots to monitor and communicate their positions on the designated CTAF when entering and exiting dedicated CTAF areas throughout Alaska, as well as near established reporting points and airport traffic patterns within the CTAF area, unless already communicating with air traffic control.

Establish additional CTAF areas in locations throughout Alaska at high risk of midair collisions, designate one frequency that is associated with all non-towered airports within the geographical boundaries of these CTAF areas, and define mandatory position reporting locations and reporting requirements within these areas.

notes: PA-12 exterior registration was N1904T (experimental), but FAA database showed valid registration N2587M
Cockpit visibility study showed PA-12 pilot had 53 seconds to see DHC-2, DHC-2 pilot had 28.3 seconds
FAA guidance indicates 12.5 seconds minimum for detection and evasive action
ATAS performance study showed if equipped, both pilots would have received alerts 26 seconds before collision
Complex visual background made detection difficult; PA-12 pilot would need to look toward sun
Entire report read to gather comprehensive accident details and recommendations
